name: Shimo
tagline: Otemachi in 32 minutes and Tokyo in 33 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Kita City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 32 minutes to Otemachi, 36 minutes to Shinjuku, 41 minutes to Shibuya and 47 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 2 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 2 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1 m to 3 m, a difference of 2 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 5 to 10 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 5 to 10 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: イオンスタイル 赤羽

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 6 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 博慈会記念総合病院, about 29 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 東京北医療センター, about 33 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Namboku Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Namboku Line runs at 156% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 駒込→本駒込, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

Whether it faces a main road or the railway

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. In plain yen, though, it is on the low side for the 23 wards. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Akabane is ahead on the number of lines and how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Shimo is ahead on quiet.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Shimo in a straight line. Akabane has 5 lines that Shimo does not. With more lines, Akabane is the better connected of the two. To Shinjuku, for instance, Akabane is 21 minutes quicker. On what it offers families, though, Shimo comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Akabane-Iwabuchi is ahead on the number of lines and the number of medical facilities, but Shimo is ahead on quiet.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Shimo in a straight line. Akabane-Iwabuchi also has the Saitama Railway Line, which Shimo does not. With more lines, Akabane-Iwabuchi is the better connected of the two. To Toranomon, for instance, Akabane-Iwabuchi takes 3 minutes longer. On what it offers families, though, Shimo comes out ahead.

noiseSources: 北本通り (3 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 6 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 4 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
